metadata.name: apt
metadata.description: Advanced Package Tool for managing software packages

installation.note: apt is built-in on Debian/Ubuntu systems by default

overview.summary: apt (Advanced Package Tool) is the modern command-line package manager for Debian and Ubuntu systems. It provides a high-level interface for managing software packages, handling installation, updates, removals, and package information. apt simplifies package management compared to the older apt-get command.

syntax.description: Package management commands. Common commands: install, update, upgrade, remove, search, show.

options.description: Show what would be done without actually doing it

misconceptions.title: apt update upgrades packages
misconceptions.reality: apt update only refreshes package lists from repositories. Use apt upgrade to actually upgrade packages. Update refreshes lists, upgrade updates packages.
misconceptions.tip: apt update = refresh package lists. apt upgrade = upgrade packages. Always run update first, then upgrade.

misconceptions.title: apt and apt-get are the same
misconceptions.misconception: apt and apt-get work exactly the same
misconceptions.reality: apt is a newer, user-friendly interface. apt-get is the older command. apt provides progress bars and better output, but apt-get is more stable for scripts.
misconceptions.tip: Use apt for interactive use (better UI). Use apt-get in scripts (more stable). Most commands are similar.

common_pitfalls.description: Most apt commands require root privileges
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo for install, update, upgrade, remove. Search and show don't need sudo.

common_pitfalls.description: Trying to upgrade without updating package lists first
common_pitfalls.solution: Always run sudo apt update before sudo apt upgrade to get latest package information.

common_pitfalls.description: Package names might differ from common names
common_pitfalls.solution: Use apt search keyword to find correct package name before installing. Package names are usually lowercase with hyphens.
Only add repositories from trusted sources. Be careful with PPAs (Personal Package Archives).

best_practices: Always run sudo apt update before installing or upgrading
Use apt search to find packages before installing
Use apt show to check package details before installing
Use sudo apt upgrade regularly to keep system updated
Use apt list --installed | grep package to check if package is installed
Review what will be installed before confirming
Use --dry-run to preview changes without applying them
performance_tips: apt update is usually fast (few seconds) - run it regularly
apt search can be slow on first run (indexes packages)
Use apt-cache search for faster package searching in some cases
apt list can be slow - pipe to grep or less for large lists

additional_notes.update_vs_upgrade: apt update refreshes package lists, apt upgrade upgrades packages. Always run update first.
additional_notes.sudo_required: Most apt commands need sudo (install, update, upgrade, remove). Search and show don't need sudo.
additional_notes.vs_apt-get: apt is newer with better UI. apt-get is older but more stable for scripts. Most commands work the same.
additional_notes.package_names: Package names are usually lowercase with hyphens. Use apt search to find correct names.
additional_notes.repositories: Packages come from repositories configured in /etc/apt/sources.list and /etc/apt/sources.list.d/
